For large negative values of $x,$ we have $|-12x+5|=-12x+5.$ Consequently, for $x\to -\infty ,$ we get

$$
\frac{|-12x+5|}{4x+3}=\frac{-12x+5}{4x+3}.
$$

First, we divide both the numerator and the denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is ${x}^{1}.$ Then, by noting that the reciprocals shrink to $0$ in the limit, we can then evaluate the resulting expression.

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{-12x+5}{4x+3} & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(\frac{-12x}{x}+\frac{5}{x})}{(\frac{4x}{x}+\frac{3}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{(-12+\frac{5}{x})}{(4+\frac{3}{x})} \\  & =\frac{-12+0}{4+0} \\  & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$
